explain.say: A thirteen-year-old village boy, Ugwu, arrives in a university town to work as houseboy for a lecturer who insists on teaching him. Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie set her 2006 novel in 1960s Nigeria, through the war over Biafra. A gentle note: it includes massacres, starvation and sexual violence. The web shows the people whose lives the war tears through.

nodes.ask: Who wrote The World Was Silent When We Died?

explain.say: Look at the history. Nigeria became independent in 1960. In 1966 thousands of Igbo people were killed in the north, and Olanna witnesses a massacre. In May 1967 the south-east declared itself the Republic of Biafra, with half of a yellow sun on its flag. Federal forces blockaded it, and famine followed. Why tell this through one household?

events.label: Independence
events.note: Nigeria is free from British rule.

events.label: Massacres
events.note: Thousands of Igbo people killed in the north.

explain.say: The novel moves back and forth. Parts one and three are in the early sixties, full of love, arguments and a painful betrayal between the twin sisters, Olanna and Kainene. Parts two and four are the late sixties, at war. Adichie holds back the cause of the twins' rift, so you live through the war with an open wound. Why build it this way?

Look at Ugwu. Forced into the Biafran army as a teenager, he takes part in an act of sexual violence he is deeply ashamed of, and Adichie does not let us look away. Later he begins writing a book about the war, The World Was Silent When We Died, whose extracts appear between chapters. Who has the right to tell this story?

explain.say: Kainene crosses enemy lines to trade for food and never returns; the novel leaves her fate open. Estimates of the war's dead range from about half a million to more than two million, most from starvation. Thank you for staying with a hard story. Challenge: why might Adichie leave Kainene's fate unknown?

draw.label: Biafra, 1967 to 1970: the breakaway south-eastern region of Nigeria, around Enugu and Nsukka

faq.a: The Republic of Biafra was the south-eastern region of Nigeria, mainly Igbo, that declared independence on 30 May 1967. After a war and a blockade that caused mass famine, it surrendered in January 1970.
After the coups of 1966 and massacres of Igbo people in northern Nigeria, many easterners felt unsafe in the federation. Talks failed, and the eastern leader Odumegwu Ojukwu declared independence.
asks: Causes of the Nigerian Civil War

faq.q: Who wrote The World Was Silent When We Died?
faq.a: The book-within-the-book is revealed at the end to be written by Ugwu. Richard, the English writer, had meant to write about the war but realises it is not his story to tell.
asks: Book within a book Half of a Yellow Sun

faq.a: Near the war's end she goes across enemy lines to trade for food and does not come back. Olanna and Richard search for her, but her fate is never revealed.

faq.q: Why is Half of a Yellow Sun told out of order?
faq.a: Its four parts alternate between the early and late 1960s, so the causes of the sisters' estrangement are revealed late. The structure builds suspense and shows how private and national histories intertwine.
asks: Structure of Half of a Yellow Sun

facts: Half of a Yellow Sun was published in 2006 and won the Orange Prize for Fiction in 2007.
Biafra declared independence on 30 May 1967; the war ended in January 1970.
The novel takes its title from the half-risen yellow sun on the Biafran flag.
